Hi Sarah / Paul,

Thanks — happy to clarify. I've attached a brief scope map (SIG_scope_map_v1.xlsx) and a short explainer below that you can paste into the SIG workbook as an appendix. Drive link is here: https://drive.google.com/example/SIG_scope_map_v1

Quick summary (high level):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood operates the full stack (control owner = Redwood) for the managed service plane: orchestration, runtime, persistent layers we control, backups we manage. Customers are responsible for their API keys, prompt/content they send, and any customer-side logging they configure. Evidence we can provide: SOC 2 scope statement, system architecture diagrams, runtime logging retention policy, control implementation narratives.

- Dedicated (Reserved GPU capacity): Infrastructure and runtime are Redwood-managed, but the customer has isolated capacity and can opt for different networking configurations. Control ownership is mixed: Redwood owns platform-level controls (compute hygiene, runtime patching, kernel selection), while customers own tenant-level configuration, secrets management (if they integrate their KMS), and can control data egress rules. Evidence we can provide for Dedicated: SOC 2 scope statement, tenancy isolation diagrams, options for customer-managed KMS integration, and operational runbooks for provisioning.

- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer-managed deployment where the customer is the primary control owner for infrastructure, physical security, and network boundaries. Redwood provides the application and control-plane artifacts and can operate under an NDA with access to support/debug logs. Evidence we can provide here is limited to software package manifests, deployment guides, and if under contract, exported audit logs and signed statements about what Redwood-operated services provide. Physical security, hardware lifecycle, and on-prem backups are the customer's responsibility.

A couple of practical notes for filling SIG columns:
- Where the workbook asks for "Control owner": mark \"Redwood\" for Hosted controls; mark \"Redwood / Customer\" for Dedicated (and add a note referencing the tenancy and KMS options); mark \"Customer\" for on-prem controls that touch physical or network perimeters.
- Where evidence is requested, attach the SOC2_scope_statement.pdf and the attached SIG_scope_map_v1.xlsx. For Dedicated, also reference the tenancy isolation diagram in the workbook (tab 2).
- Logging/retention: Hosted retains service-level operational logs as per our retention policy; customers can request longer retention or export via our logging hooks if on Dedicated or Private.

I've attached: SIG_scope_map_v1.xlsx (mapping table) and SOC2_scope_statement.pdf. If you'd like, I can add a short canned text you can paste into the SIG "Scope statement" cell.

Hi all,

Adding a couple technical clarifications from Security: 
- Logging/Retention: For Hosted, we retain service operational logs for 365 days by default (system metrics, runtime events). For Dedicated we can offer configurable retention up to 3 years depending on contract; retention beyond default is typically exported to customer-managed storage. For Private/on-prem, retention is entirely customer-controlled.
- Key Management: Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS by default; Dedicated: optional customer-managed KMS integration (customer-side keys can be used for dataset encryption at rest); Private: customer-managed HSM/KMS.
- Evidence bundles: SOC2_scope_statement.pdf covers our Hosted and Dedicated controls in-scope; for Private deployments we provide software manifests and a signed scope statement on request under NDA.

I've uploaded a short note (SOC2_scope_statement.pdf) to the Drive link Hannah shared. Happy to walk Globex through any of the artifacts if needed.

Regards,
Monica Patel
